rationale: X proposes the right oracle-and-observation approach and covers all requested categories, but several of its fixed expected values disagree with the checked-out implementation. Most importantly, its custom multibyte omission table drops graphemes that fit exactly, so replaying this strategy would falsely report a behavior-preserving refactor as broken. The encoding section also pairs a three-byte within-budget receiver with impossible truncated outputs, making the strategy less reliable than the references.
shortcomings: The custom-omission table expects `"👍🖖"` at budget 12 and only `"🖖"` at budget 8. The loop at activesupport/lib/active_support/core_ext/string/filters.rb:140-146 uses `<= cut_at`, so two thumbs fit before the 4-byte omission at 12 and one fits at 8; the focused command returned `n=12: "👍👍🖖" (12)` and `n=8: "👍🖖" (8)`. These wrong oracle values directly undermine the proposed deterministic verification.

Under encoding preservation, X defines a three-byte US-ASCII `"abc"` and then says the same string truncated to budget 5 yields `"abcd."` with a custom omission and `"ab…"` with the default. Because `bytesize <= truncate_to` is the first branch at activesupport/lib/active_support/core_ext/string/filters.rb:130-131, both calls return a duplicate `"abc"` in US-ASCII; the focused command confirmed exactly that.
strengths: X's thread did run a broad probe against the current method and captured content, bytesize, encoding, class, identity, validity, and receiver state across many branches (X.thread.md, the `/tmp/truncate_bytes_probe.rb` command and output), which is stronger investigation than relying on source inspection alone.
